note: Extends examples/velantra.json no-bnpl (Klarna/Afterpay/Affirm/Shop Pay installments). Velantra does not offer buy-now-pay-later: no Zip badge, no 'Shop Now, Pay Later', no 'Pay later with...'. Strip payment-method rows from Nuamore-style references like competitor logos.

Default: no brand is ever named in Velantra copy; designer talk stays category-level ('designer prices', 'designer inflation'). Hermès stays out ALWAYS. Other houses are allowed only in a Brooks-directed comparison-FORMAT ad (ranked roundup), praised sincerely with a trade-off never a defect, prices verified same day from the brand's own site. Extends no-competitor-names.

law: Birkin never enters a generation prompt
note: 'Birkin-inspired' is live VO/caption vocabulary for the Weekender, Vivienne, Sofia and Inspired Birkin, but it NEVER appears in an image or video generation prompt. The kie runner's claims-grep hard-fails the job. Prompts describe the silhouette from the product-truth identity block instead.

law: Birkin is a lineage claim, never 'is a Birkin'
note: A caption card reading 'It's a Birkin' (split off from '-inspired shape') claims the bag IS a Birkin, a counterfeit-adjacent claim. 'Birkin' must carry '-inspired' in the SAME card / sentence. 'The Birkin is your dream bag' (hook about the icon) is allowed and does not match.
Birkin-inspired is a lineage claim about our silhouette, never a price comparison. No Birkin price is ever quoted; never a price-led 'dupe for less'.

law: no dupe / replica / knockoff / alternative wording
note: The words dupe / replica / alternative / knockoff never appear in Velantra copy. Lead with architecture and identity. DMCA history (luxboattote) makes this a store-survival issue, not a taste issue.

law: never say the phrase 'quiet luxury' in copy
note: REGISTER = quiet luxury (Brooks 2026-07-23) uses restraint vocabulary ('quietly', 'chose restraint', 'without ceremony') but never names the phrase; naming it breaks it.

law: 'affordable luxury' is internal mechanism language, not customer-facing copy
note: 'Affordable luxury' is internal-only, never spoken in customer-facing copy (2026-07-23). The 2026-07-28 update ('Affordable luxury is fine. The problem is the scam position.') approved the VALUE positioning; whether the literal phrase may now appear in copy is ambiguous, so this stays a warning. Counter-promise wording: 'quality that actually matches the price'.

law: designer-inflation language: no 'tired of X' complaint structure
note: Meaning beats are observational and identity-forward (who she is, what she noticed, what we promise), never grievance. 'We got tired of it' / 'Women are tired of feeling scammed' were rewritten before production. Reaffirmed 2026-07-28 when Brooks chose discernment framing over direct 'tired of' language.

law: designer-inflation language: never priced out / can't afford / bitter
note: The identity to emulate is the woman who is NOT frivolously spending on designer: she could, she chooses not to. Sour-grapes framing repels her. The can't-afford reality can inform targeting internally but never appears in customer-facing copy.

law: comparison-ad tone: competitors get a trade-off, never a defect
note: Banned in any Velantra comparison ad: 'the whole bag', 'that is all it is', sneering, or any framing where a rival's bag is the problem. Test: if a line would make a Saint Laurent owner feel stupid, it is the wrong line; she is the avatar. Thesis line: 'the only question is how much of what you are paying for is actually the bag.'

law: no object personification / no fourth-wall on the muse names
note: Never call the product line 'the women', never state bags are named for / are women, never 'The women aren't real. The lives are.' Anywhere: decks, briefs, PDPs, ads. A bare 'the women' is too common to regex; read for it. Vestirsi model: the name is just a name.

law: no epithet tag lines on the muse names
note: Epithets ('the summer one', 'the everyday one', 'the polished one', 'the one that never checks a bag') lower perceived value and state the obvious (Brooks 2026-07-23). PDP: name = title only, body opens on craft/function copy.

Velantra bags are manufactured in China. Never claim US/EU/Italian manufacture. Approved framing: 'Designed in the U.S., handcrafted by skilled artisans overseas.' Extends examples/velantra.json no-origin-claims with the inherited-claim sweep terms (Italian/Tuscan/tannery/LWG). CARVE-OUT: the material line 'softest Italian leather' is APPROVED in Straw Tote ad scripts and must not be auto-stripped; note that the existing no-origin-claims regex ('italian\s+leather') will flag it as a warning.

law: Jessica persona RETIRED; Brooks is the public founder
note: Since 2026-07-22 Brooks is the public founder in ALL customer-facing copy; sign founder letters 'Brooks, Founder'. Never resurrect Jessica (cleanup debt remains in old Omnisend templates / sender names).

law: locked founding claim: 'Founded in Newport Beach'
note: 'Founded in Newport Beach' superseded the earlier same-day Nantucket phrasing (2026-07-23). Founding claim only; never extended to where bags are made.

Two prompt phrasings actively cause the open-straw-box failure on the Straw Tote / Weekender: describing the mouth as 'visible rising above and behind the flap', and any wording implying the interior should be shown. The flap folds over the ENTIRE bag; a packing shot looks CLOSED.

law: Seedance cannot spell 'Weekender' as native text
note: Seedance renders 'Weekender' as Weekaner/Weekaver. Strip the caption from the prompt and post-overlay via Pillow PNG. Native two-line captions must not use periods as line delimiters; pin size/position explicitly.
